synopsis: Chapter 12 presents Amazon's six-page narrative and PR/FAQ as practitioner formats for executive communication, alongside other planning and decision frameworks [f9851]. The glossary explains working backwards as writing a product press release before building the product, then adding frequently asked questions with honest answers [f16456]. The narrative memo is a sibling of working backwards, with a documented six-page limit, and is read silently at the start of a meeting instead of using slides [f9989, f16458]. The supplied facts describe these formats but do not establish their effectiveness for the collision-mitigation validation plan [f9851, f16456, f9989, f16458].

relations.note: Explains the press-release-first process behind the listed Amazon PR/FAQ format.
Identifies six pages as a documented limit, not merely a format name.
Adds silent meeting reading and replacement of slides to the narrative format.
Both identify the Amazon narrative memo as six pages.
Connects working backwards to its sibling narrative memo and meeting practice.
